Let the preceding wave be nonzero and transverse over continuous trace-free $B$, with positive activation strength $\sigma$ and couplings $
u,\eta$, and let $E_c$ be continuous. Set $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$, $S=\sigma/r$, $\varepsilon=\eta/
u$ and $	au=r(t-t_0)$. On a compact physical set $I$ containing $[t_0,t_0+T/r]$, define $\delta=\|B_{12}/
u-1\|_\infty+\|B_{32}/\eta-1\|_\infty+\|B\|_\infty/r+\|E_c\|_\infty/
u$. The formal statement assumes $T\ge2$, sufficiently large integer $C_0$, $C_0\varepsilon\le1$ and $C_0T^{C_0}\delta\le\varepsilon$. The new wave solves $k'=-(B+\mathbf a_p\otimes k_p+E_c)^Tk$ and starts at $\lambda E_3$, $\lambda>0$.

It retains both bounds in (2.10), the bounds $1/2\le\zeta_3\le3/2$ and $|\zeta|\le3T^2$, and the reduced amplitude equation with exactly the reference matrix in the paper’s coordinates $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)$. There is one error operator $\mathcal E(	au)$ for all transverse amplitude vectors. Its bound is $CT^p\delta$, where the real factor $C$ and nonnegative integer exponent $p$ are chosen before the sufficiently large threshold for $C_0$ and before all wave data. The common bound is at most $1/2$. The formal statement additionally asserts continuity of $\mathcal E$ and $|\sigma_p/\sigma-1|\le2T\delta$, properties obtained in the paper’s proof but omitted from its displayed lemma statement.

The norms of $B,E_c$ are Euclidean operator norms on $\mathbb R^3$; the norm of $\mathcal E$ is the operator norm for the maximum norm on pairs. The paper leaves these matrix norms unspecified. Taking $I$ to be exactly the active physical interval reproduces its supremum domain; enlarging $I$ can increase $\delta$ and imposes a correspondingly stronger smallness condition. These domain and norm choices are part of the comparison, not suppressed conventions.
